questions.question: Define government and explain, with two examples, why some goods are provided by government rather than by private businesses.
questions.expected_answer: Government is the group of people and institutions with the authority to make, carry out and judge the laws of a country, and to provide public goods and services. Public goods such as street lights and national defence are non-excludable and non-rival: once supplied, everyone benefits and non-payers cannot easily be kept out, so a profit-making business could not charge for them and would not supply them (the free-rider problem). Government pays for them from taxes. It also provides essential services such as basic education and clean water so that people who cannot pay the full price still receive them.

questions.question: Name the three spheres of government in South Africa, the leader of the executive in each, and two services each one is responsible for.
questions.expected_answer: National: the President with the Cabinet; responsible for, for example, defence (SANDF), policing (SAPS), Home Affairs documents, social grants through SASSA, tax collection through SARS. Provincial: the Premier with MECs; responsible for public schools, public hospitals and clinics, provincial roads, housing programmes. Local: the mayor with the municipal council and ward councillors; responsible for water and sanitation, refuse removal, electricity distribution, municipal roads, street lights, parks and libraries.

questions.question: Explain the separation of powers. Name the three arms of government, state the function of each and give the national body that performs it.
questions.expected_answer: The separation of powers divides state power between three arms so that no single person or group controls everything and each can check the others. The legislature makes laws: Parliament (National Assembly and National Council of Provinces). The executive carries out laws and runs government departments: the President and Cabinet. The judiciary interprets laws and settles disputes: the courts, with the Constitutional Court highest on constitutional matters. This prevents abuse of power and protects citizens' rights.
